explain.say: Close your eyes for a moment. How do you know if it is raining outside, or if dinner is ready? Your body has five senses that are always detecting things. Look at the face on the board. Let's be sense detectives!

explain.say: See the Seeing group lighting up? Your eyes tell you about a rainbow, traffic lights and a friend's smile. Can you spot three red things near you right now? That is your eyes working!
Now Hearing glows. Your ears catch thunder, a doorbell and birdsong, even with your eyes shut. Listen hard: what is the quietest sound you can hear right now?

Here are Smelling and Tasting, best friends. Your nose sniffs smoke, bread and jasmine, and smells help you taste. Hold your nose and eat a crisp: it tastes of almost nothing! Have you noticed food tastes dull when you have a cold?

Last, see the skin lighting up. Skin is your touch sense, all over your body, feeling hot, cold, soft and sharp. Great detecting! Wow fact: skin is your biggest organ, and it covers about two square metres on a grown-up, about the size of a single bed sheet.

faq.a: The five senses are sight with your eyes, hearing with your ears, smell with your nose, taste with your tongue and touch with your skin.

faq.q: Why can I not taste food when my nose is blocked?
faq.a: Much of what we call flavour actually comes from smell. When your nose is blocked, smells cannot reach it, so food tastes dull and your tongue only notices sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury.
asks: Why does food taste bland when I have a cold?

faq.q: What is the biggest sense organ?
faq.a: Your skin. It covers your whole body, about two square metres on an adult, and is full of tiny sensors for touch, pressure, heat, cold and pain.

faq.q: How do senses keep us safe?
faq.a: Senses warn us of danger: we smell smoke, hear a car horn, see a red light, taste food that has gone bad and feel a hot pan before we get badly hurt.

faq.q: What tastes can the tongue notice?
faq.a: The tongue notices five basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami, a savoury taste found in foods like tomatoes, cheese and soy sauce.

facts: An adult's skin covers about 1.5 to 2 square metres.
The tongue detects five basic tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami.

quiz.say: You hear a doorbell ring. Which sense did you use?
quiz.show: A doorbell uses your sense of…
quiz.why: Sounds are detected by your ears, your sense of hearing.

wrong.0: Sight uses your eyes; you can hear a doorbell with your eyes shut.
wrong.2: Taste uses your tongue, not for sounds.

quiz.say: Why does food taste dull when your nose is blocked?
quiz.show: Food tastes dull with a blocked nose because…
quiz.why: A lot of flavour comes from smell, so a blocked nose makes food taste dull.

wrong.1: The tongue still works; it is the smell that is missing.
wrong.2: The food is the same; your nose just cannot smell it.
